content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: The notice lists the following eligibility conditions for the Post-Doctoral Fellow (PDF): The applicant must be an Indian citizen. The applicant must possess a PhD degree from a recognized university, with first class (or equivalent grades) at all preceding academic levels and a consistently good academic record. The PhD must have been completed within the five years immediately preceding the last date for submission of the application to NERIST. The applicant must have a proven record of research, supported by peer-reviewed publications, recognitions and/or relevant research outputs in ESDM or IT/ITES. The applicant must not have obtained the PhD degree from NERIST, the proposed host institution. Applicants in regular employment are not eligible. Researchers holding temporary academic or research appointments may be considered, but must relinquish the existing position upon selection and before joining. An applicant already receiving any other fellowship from a government or non-government source is not eligible to receive it concurrently with this PDF award. The applicant must not exceed 40 years of age on the date of submission of the application to NERIST. The notice does not mention any age relaxation. A suitable mentor/guide must be identified by the host institution. The mentor must hold a regular academic/research position in a recognized Indian institution and possess a PhD in Science or Engineering. The research proposal must clearly specify objectives, methodology, expected outcomes, milestones and measurable deliverables within the fellowship tenure. Preference may be accorded to applicants with active industry linkages and research proposals addressing industry-specific problems. NERIST may prescribe additional shortlisting criteria consistent with the applicable scheme guidelines; meeting the minimum criteria does not guarantee an interview or selection. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions before applying.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: The fellowship is tenable in India only, at the host institution to which the PDF seat is allotted. The initial tenure is one year. Any extension, if permitted, is subject to performance review and approval by the PhD Cell, Digital India Corporation (DIC), MeitY, under the applicable scheme provisions. The travel support covers (a) visa fee and one-time travel support for eligible overseas faculty/applicants returning to India to take up the fellowship, and (b) participation in invited Visvesvaraya scheme activities/events/workshops. The contingency grant may be used for eligible minor equipment, consumables and other research-related expenditure in accordance with the scheme. The host institution is expected to provide administrative and infrastructure support. No separate research personnel support is provided; the fellow is expected to perform the approved research personally. All financial benefits and tenure conditions remain subject to fund availability, sanctioned seats and the latest guidelines of the Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme. The PDF is a full-time assignment and shall not be held simultaneously with another fellowship or a full-time/part-time employment assignment. The fellowship is temporary, non-transferable and confined to the host institution where the PDF seat is allocated and the fellow is enrolled. The fellow shall work under the approved mentor and adhere to the approved research plan, reporting requirements, financial rules and institutional regulations. The fellow must not claim regular employment or automatic absorption in NERIST by virtue of holding the fellowship. Discontinuation or resignation is dealt with under the scheme; the reference guidelines specify one month's advance notice by the institution to the PhD Cell, DIC, MeitY. No expenditure may be incurred after the effective date of resignation or termination. The PhD Cell, DIC, MeitY may withhold, stop or discontinue support for inadequate research progress, improper utilization of grants or non-compliance, and may revise the terms; the latest approved scheme guidelines prevail.

Detailed research proposal describing the background, objectives, methods, work plan, milestones, outcomes and deliverables. Copies (first pages) of selected publications and patents, evidence of industry collaboration and other supporting testimonials. Category/PwBD certificate and GATE/NET/GPAT or other scorecards, if applicable. No-objection or undertaking to relinquish a temporary appointment, if applicable. Proof of payment of the application fee. Transfer, migration or conduct certificate and Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) ID may be required by NERIST at joining, along with any additional documents specified in the interview call letter.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Applications will be scrutinized by a duly constituted NERIST committee in accordance with the sanctioned PDF seats and scheme guidelines. Candidates may be shortlisted on academic record, PhD research relevance, quality of publications, research proposal, proposed mentor alignment and other approved criteria. Shortlisted applicants will be informed through the official NERIST channel, ordinarily by email, and may be called for an interview/presentation of the proposed research. Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents and one set of self-attested photocopies for verification at the interview or joining stage. The selection committee shall recommend suitable candidate(s) to the competent authority, subject to scheme approvals and verification of documents. Candidates called for an in-person interview make their own travel and accommodation arrangements, and no TA/DA will be paid, unless NERIST expressly notifies otherwise.

faq.question: Q1. What is the last date to apply for the NERIST Post-Doctoral Fellow 2026?
faq.answer: Applications must be received through email by 26.11.2026.

faq.question: Q2. What qualification is required for the NERIST PDF?
faq.answer: A PhD degree from a recognized university, completed within the five years before the last date, with first class (or equivalent grades) at all preceding levels and a proven research record in ESDM or IT/ITES.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit for the NERIST Post-Doctoral Fellow?
faq.answer: The applicant must not exceed 40 years of age on the date of submission of the application to NERIST.

faq.question: Q4. How much is the NERIST PDF fellowship per month?
faq.answer: The monthly fellowship is ₹1,08,393 (₹13,00,716 for 12 months), with a contingency grant of ₹1,00,000 per year and travel support up to ₹2,10,000 subject to scheme approval.

faq.question: Q5. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: A non-refundable fee of ₹1500.00 plus bank transaction charges applies to all candidates, irrespective of category, paid to the NERIST Academic Fee A/C at State Bank of India.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply and what subject line should I use?
faq.answer: Email the signed form with self-attested enclosures as one consolidated PDF to [email protected] with the subject "Application for Visvesvaraya PDF – <Your Name>".

faq.question: Q7. How will candidates be selected?
faq.answer: A NERIST committee scrutinizes applications and shortlists candidates, who may be called for an interview/presentation of the proposed research on 30.11.2026, followed by document verification.

faq.question: Q8. Is the NERIST PDF a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. The fellowship is full-time, temporary and non-transferable with an initial tenure of one year, and gives no claim to regular employment or absorption in NERIST.

faq.question: Q9. Can a candidate with a PhD from NERIST apply?
faq.answer: No. Applicants who obtained their PhD from NERIST, those in regular employment, and those receiving another fellowship concurrently are not eligible.

faq.question: Q10. Will TA/DA be paid for the interview?
faq.answer: No TA/DA will be paid for attending the interview unless NERIST expressly notifies otherwise.
